summary: Verified Chrome MV3 extension packaging fix. /app/frontend/public/concon-extension.zip has manifest.json at archive top level; JSON is valid with manifest_version=3; all 14 files referenced by the manifest (1 content script, 12 web_accessible_resources, 1 background service_worker) exist at their declared relative paths after extraction. Fallback /app/frontend/public/concon.zip still contains concon/extension/manifest.json as expected. The extension-only zip is correctly structured for Chrome's Load unpacked flow after standard Windows Explorer extraction.
critical_code_review_comments: concon-extension.zip contains empty directory entries (src/, src/panel/, src/core/, src/background/, src/content/). Harmless for Chrome Load unpacked, but could be omitted from the archive for cleanliness.
Consider adding an icons/ directory and manifest 'icons' + 'action.default_icon' entries — currently missing; Chrome will use a default puzzle-piece icon.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Extension packaging is validated. If manifest changes, re-run: unzip -l /app/frontend/public/concon-extension.zip and validate that top-level entry is manifest.json (not a nested folder), then extract and confirm every path in content_scripts.js, web_accessible_resources.resources, background.service_worker exists.
rca of the issue: User selected outer /app/concon/ folder in Chrome Load unpacked; Chrome requires the folder that DIRECTLY contains manifest.json (which was /app/concon/extension/). Fix packaged a second zip with manifest.json at the archive root so extraction yields a directly-loadable folder. Verified structurally correct.
